University of Adelaide · Campaign work

Campaigns

Group pitchPromotional Culture

LoopBottle: launching a smart water bottle to uni students

We pitched a launch campaign for a bottle and app that track every sip. The key choice was framing hydration as focus, not health: "Your brain's running on 60%. Top up!"

  • Audience. Primary persona Maya, 20, a second-year student who trusts creators more than ads. Secondary: gym-goers and young professionals.
  • Channels. TikTok and Instagram micro-creators, campus refill-station activations, Spotify study-playlist audio, gym partners, and app push notifications written as mini ads.
  • 10-week rollout. Tease, launch, a #LoopStreak 30-day challenge, then "Top up before the exam does" in exam week.
  • My critical analysis. I wrote an individual analysis of the pitch's framing, symbolic value and the risks around health data and wellness pressure.
IndividualDesign · Public awareness

Your Image, Your Choice: a four-poster eSafety campaign

A public-awareness series on image-based abuse covering consent, bystanders, survivor support and the law. Each poster carries a headline, one statistic, a checklist and a call to action to esafety.gov.au. I moved the palette away from a clinical teal to colour-coded blocks, replaced an icon people misread as a smiley face, used symbols instead of faces to avoid stereotyping, and checked every statistic against eSafety Commissioner and Australian Institute of Criminology research.

Brand strategyConsumer research

Tasting Australia: a digital plan for South Australia's food and wine festival

Prepared for the Adelaide Economic Development Agency. Tasting Australia runs 150+ events over 10 days for about 65,000 people but sits behind the Fringe and Gather Round in recognition. I wrote the mobile marketing and AR/VR/AI sections and formatted the final report.

Festival app

QR codes at venues and the Town Square hub feed one app that holds tickets, maps and offers.

Geo-targeted push

Push and SMS to opted-in foodies within 25 km of any event that isn't sold out in its final 48 hours.

AR, VR and AI

An AR food trail, an AI itinerary planner and VR teasers to reach interstate visitors before they book.

KPIs

Push click-through, AR activations, app downloads, geofence conversions and social reach.

University of Adelaide · Strategy and analytics

Research & analysis

Individual · Python, Excel, Tableau

What drives restaurant ratings?

I cleaned 51,717 Zomato listings down to 9,438 unique venues and ran a regression that explains 41.8% of the variation in ratings. Price looked like it mattered on its own, but the effect disappeared once table booking and popularity were included. My recommendation: invest in reservations before discounting. I built the Tableau dashboard so a manager can filter by cuisine, price band and booking.

PythonRegressionTableauExcel pivots

Individual · Marketing plan

Move Physiotherapy situation analysis

An audit of a struggling two-physio clinic. Awareness was 2% against 61% for the market leader, visits were down 57%, and revenue was tracking at 14% of the owners' goal. I sized the local market at about £1.66M a year and costed each channel, finding a new patient from Google search costs about £50 but is worth about £143.

SWOTPESTELMedia audit

Individual · Social media

Gymshark content analysis

I compared five Gymshark posts across TikTok and Instagram and normalised their engagement. A trend-led "Winter Arc" TikTok earned 25.6% engagement per view, almost five times a post featuring Sam Sulek (5.5%). Its 22.1K saves and 15.8K shares showed people meant to come back to it and pass it on.
